structured_output.analysis: The best grid iso_3.15 (KL 0.43614, E514ab09c524e) is at about 3.14795 avg bits against a 3.1484 budget, so there are almost no spare bits. In every top-loss layer the method already in use is the lowest-KL choice at its bit width, so no same-width swap helps. The gains that remain are upgrading int3 MLP layers to int4, e.g. 27.up 0.00572 to 0.00217 and 3.up 0.00642 to 0.00238. Paying for that by dropping another int3 layer to int2 costs about 0.02 or more per layer (e.g. 3.up rht_gptq_int2 0.0302), which cancels the gain. The ways left are bit-free option changes (act_order) or freeing bits with a larger group_size on the 109 rht_gptq_int3 layers.

proposals.name: actorder_all
proposals.rationale: No bit cost. The loss sits in GPTQ-quantized MLP layers: 27.up gptq_int3 0.0057182 (Ef04d8aa7bded), 3.up rht_gptq_int3 0.0064177 (E6f4f7ea296d5), 14.down rht_gptq_int2 0.00633466 (E4c3f9b73e065). This tests act_order=true on every GPTQ variant, starting from iso_3.15 at KL 0.43614 (E514ab09c524e).

proposals.name: gs256_rht3_up4
proposals.rationale: Uses group_size=256 on rht_gptq_int3 to free scale bits and spends them on four int4 upgrades: 27.up gptq_int3 0.0057182 (Ef04d8aa7bded) to gptq_int4 0.00216589 (Efea8c18d2abc); 3.up rht_gptq_int3 0.0064177 (E6f4f7ea296d5) to gptq_int4 0.00237732 (Ef4ee8cb4969e); 2.up gptq_int3 0.00641875 (E9baa10763ebe) to gptq_int4 0.00237045 (Ef3d9c7b4502c); 27.gate rht_gptq_int3 0.00498703 (Efa0bb391da67) to rht_gptq_int4 0.00153131 (Ef428ac081334).

proposals.name: gs256_rht3_up4_actorder
proposals.rationale: Same upgrades as gs256_rht3_up4 (27.up 0.0057182 Ef04d8aa7bded to 0.00216589 Efea8c18d2abc; 27.gate 0.00498703 Efa0bb391da67 to 0.00153131 Ef428ac081334), plus act_order=true on every GPTQ variant to offset the coarser group_size=256 on rht_gptq_int3.
